title: Roll a filled 18.5 kg glazed planter across a patio on the edge of its foot, onto a taped spot
instruction: Move the planter onto the taped square on the patio.
context: Moving a filled patio planter is an everyday garden chore. A 14-inch glazed pot full of moist potting mix weighs about 18.5 kg, and paving guides say to lift planters rather than drag them across the slabs. Without a dolly, people tip the pot onto the edge of its foot and roll it. Both hands on the rim hold it against falling back upright (about 7.8 N m at 22 degrees) and turn it like a steering wheel, staying well short of its 37-degree tipping point.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of a sturdy table. Positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm; heights are above the table. Patio: two grey porcelain pavers, 60 x 60 x 2 cm (about 16 kg each), laid side by side across the table with a 5 mm grouted joint along x at y 0, near edges at x 16, far edges at x 76, spanning y -60.75 to +60.75; they don't move. Planter: an At Home 'Rolled White Ceramic Outdoor Planter, Large', white-glazed ceramic, glazed rolled lip 35.6 cm across and 3.2 cm thick, 30.5 cm tall, body 32.9 cm across at its widest (21 cm up), opening 29.2 cm inside the lip, unglazed foot ring 20 cm across with a rounded heel; 10.1 kg empty, filled with moist potting mix to 5 cm below the rim (about 15 L, 8.4 kg), 18.5 kg in all, centre of mass 15 cm up its axis. It stands upright on the left paver, foot centre at (48, 12). Spot: 24 mm blue painter's tape on the right paver, a 40 cm square (inner edges 20 cm from its centre) around a cross 8 cm across, cross centre at (48, -12), 24 cm to the planter's right. Distractors, loose, ignored by the scoring: sunglasses (14.5 x 17.4 x 5.7 cm, plastic, 30 g) lying on the far left of the left paver at (68, 48); a glazed ceramic mug (11.4 x 9.0 x 8.0 cm, 350 g) on the far right of the right paver at (68, -48); a plastic bottle of water (6.8 cm across, 24.5 cm tall, 550 g) on the table beyond the pavers at (83, -34).
scoring: Read every control step (20 Hz). 0 for the rest of the trial if the planter ever tilts more than 32 degrees from vertical, if the lowest point of its foot ever rises more than 1 cm above the pavers (lifted), or if its foot has slid more than 10 cm in total across the pavers (the foot point touching the pavers, followed from each step to the next and added up; rolling leaves that point in place, dragging moves it). Otherwise the planter counts only while standing: axis within 2 degrees of vertical, foot centre within 3 mm of the paver tops, moving under 1 cm/s and turning under 3 degrees/s, every fingertip at least 5 cm from it. Standing, its foot centre within 3 cm of the tape cross for 1 s: 1.0. Standing, foot centre within 8 cm of the cross (also while that 1 s runs): 0.5. Standing, foot centre at least 10 cm closer to the cross than at the start (24 cm away): 0.25. Not standing, or none of these: 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Real trial: from overhead and side video and a phone inclinometer on the planter's inner wall (most tilt, lift, slide, stillness, hands clear); at the end, before anyone touches it, a steel rule laid flat from the foot to the square's inner tape edge on all four sides gives the foot centre's offset from the cross.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Roll the planter back onto its start circle (a 20 cm pencil circle at (48, 12)). Before each trial, weigh it on a bathroom scale (18.5 +/- 0.5 kg; add or let dry potting mix) and check the mix is 5 cm below the rim.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies at 240 Hz. The planter is one rigid body of convex hulls from a lathe profile estimated from the listing; the mix is part of it (no spill or shift). Real size; 18.5 kg (listed 10.1 kg pot plus 15 L of mix at 0.56 kg/L). Foot and pavers: friction 0.7/0.6. The pavers are one fixed slab; the tape is only visual. Nothing breaks or scratches: tipping, lifting and dragging are read from the pot's pose. Planter and pavers are custom meshes; distractors are SimReady props.
